A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalFM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison; moved and renumbered material can be matched without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original CausalFM experiments on synthetic CATE datasets, semi-synthetic Jobs and ACIC2016 data, and instrumental-variable and front-door settings, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds identification-strategy ablations, confounding-strength sensitivity results, and runtime comparisons in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The SCM/cluster-BNN prior construction, interventional negative-log-likelihood training, transformer architecture, and Gaussian-mixture output remain unchanged. The new input-format explanation and alternative-prior ablations do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic standard CATE estimation, Jobs, ACIC2016, binary and continuous IVs, and front-door adjustment. The new analyses reuse these causal settings; incorrect model assumptions and an explicit confounding-strength sweep do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 2–8 retain their baseline membership, including the three plug-in front-door learners and DoPFN. The new runtime tables use existing comparator sets, while Table 9 compares internal prior configurations rather than introducing another baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: Appendix H.5 adds correct-versus-incorrect identification-design controls and a confounding-strength sweep over alpha in [0,1]. H.6 introduces runtime measurement using inference alone for foundation models and training plus inference for conventional estimators. Previously documented splits, PEHE evaluation, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's benchmark comparisons across confounding strengths, v3 directly tests the consequences of using an incorrect back-door prior on IV and front-door data (Table 9). Figure 2 adds explicit sensitivity curves across confounding strength. These substantially extend empirical scrutiny of the framework's central prior-design assumptions.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 retains five repetitions with different random seeds, and existing aggregate tables retain mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or revised repetition counts are documented. The changed standard deviation in Table 4 is a result update.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive diagnostic and runtime results in Figure 2 and Tables 9–11. Table 9 reports correct-versus-back-door PEHE of 0.422 versus 0.489 for IV and 0.847 versus 0.876 for front-door data. Table 4 changes CausalFM from 0.901±0.20 to 0.847±0.34, moving its reported mean below the unchanged neural plug-in baseline's 0.889±0.38, without explaining the revision. Tables 2–3 and 5–8 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 replaces v2's global non-cancellation condition with an explicit condition within each observational-equivalence class. Appendix C.1 substantially revises the derivation through normalized prior masses, integral decomposition, and explicit consistency and integrability requirements. This changes the central theorem's assumptions and mathematical reasoning; the Appendix B lemmas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: identifiable SCM-based priors, Bayesian PFN training, and competitive inference without dataset-specific retraining across three causal settings. Although v3 removes the standalone conclusion, its substantive framework and applicability claims remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that evaluation is limited to synthetic and semi-synthetic data and proposes applied A/B evaluation (Section 6.4). It adds sensitivity-analysis guidance for suspected identification violations and interprets the new ablations and confounding sweep as evidence about prior correctness and robustness. These refine v2's existing identifiability discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds CausalFM Toolkit and documentation access links alongside the retained project-code link, plus a reproducibility statement. Appendix D.1 newly explains context datasets, query inputs, and single-forward-pass prediction. Existing architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures, and data-generation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against Dhir et al. (2025), citing neural processes, and the identification discussion adds sensitivity-analysis references. New Appendix A.1 expands comparisons with CausalPFN and Do-PFN, largely developing distinctions already present in v2 rather than redefining the paper's research position.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized structural changes: front-door details move to Appendix H.1, discussion replaces the standalone conclusion, and ethics, reproducibility, and comparative-explanation passages are added. The header changes to ICLR 2026 publication status. Most existing narrative and terminology remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the sensitivity plot in Figure 2 and Tables 9–11, enlarges and repositions the unchanged C-DAG graphic in Figure 1, and reflows existing tables and surrounding text. These are localized display additions and layout adjustments; existing table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new identification-assumption checks and runtime measurements strengthen empirical support, while explicit applicability limits and toolkit/input documentation improve usability. These address gaps in v2. The gain is limited by sparse protocol details for the new analyses, an unexplained front-door score revision, and a conditioning error that remains in the rewritten proof's Appendix C.1, Eq. (17).
